# coverage_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Measure the library's test coverage and report where it falls short.

## Synopsis

```text
coverage_tool <action> [options]
```

## Description

Actions:

- `run`: run the unit tests under coverage.py the way CI does (from the checkout,
  `pytest -q -c Tests/pytest.ini Tests/unit`, with pyproject's `[tool.coverage]`
  settings), then report. The data is kept in the cache's `Coverage` directory, not
  the checkout.
- `report`: report on the last measurement without running anything.

The library report gives the overall figure against the floor CI enforces (read
from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), a table per area (`core` for top-level modules,
otherwise the first package such as `cli` or `emulators`), the files missing the
most statements, the functions no test runs at all, and the files with nothing run.

With `-m`, the report covers one module instead: its untested line ranges and every
function with untested lines, whether never or partly run. `--source` adds each of
those functions' source with its untested lines marked `!!`, which is also a compact
brief to attach to `llm_chat` when asking a model how to test them.

Every number comes from coverage.py's own data; functions are found by parsing the
source, and a line counts toward the innermost function that holds it.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `<action>` | Action to perform: `run` or `report`. Default: `report`. |
| `-m, --module <module>` | Report on this module alone, e.g. `programs.py` or `cli/backup_tool.py`. |
| `-n, --limit <limit>` | Rows in each ranked table of the library report. Default: `20`. |
| `-o, --output_file <output_file>` | Also write the report to this Markdown file. |
| `--source` | With `-m`, include the source of each function with untested lines. |
| `--integration` | With `run`, measure the integration tests as well. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Measure and report on the whole library

```bash
coverage_tool run
```

### Report again on the last measurement

```bash
coverage_tool report
```

### Show the 40 files missing the most

```bash
coverage_tool report -n 40
```

### Detail one module

```bash
coverage_tool report -m programs.py
```

### Detail one module with its untested source

```bash
coverage_tool report -m collection/jsondata.py --source
```

### Save the report as Markdown

```bash
coverage_tool report -o coverage.md
```

### Ask a local model how to test a module

```bash
coverage_tool report -m programs.py --source -o brief.md && llm_chat --code -a brief.md
```

## Notes

- coverage.py comes with the dev extra, which the bootstrap's `python` component installs.
- `run` exits with an error when a test fails, after printing the report, since the numbers then
  reflect a broken run.
- `--integration` adds `Tests/integration`, whose tests need programs outside the process; CI does
  not run them, so its figure differs.
- A module name matches the end of a measured file's path, such as `programs.py` or
  `cli/backup_tool.py`.
